name: Cerealius
bio: Cerealius is one of the named epigrammatists whose short poems are preserved in the Greek Anthology. Paton's Index of Authors says the poet's date is unknown.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the fourth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XI: 129, 144.

poems.title: Book XI, 129
poems.author: Cerealius
poems.text: A PorT coming to the Isthmian games to the contest, when he found other poets there said he had paristhmia (mumps). He is going to start off for the Pythian games, and if he finds poets there again he can’t say he has parapythia as well.

poems.title: Book XI, 144
poems.author: Cerealius
poems.text: To use magniloquent words and four or five Attic ones is not to study with proper fervour and wisdom. For not even if you say “quaked,” and “clangs,’ and “ hisses,” and “ gurgled,” will you be a Homer at once. Sense should underlie literature, and its phraseology be more vulgar so that people may understand what you say.
